messages.author: 7797bf0ba5995253
messages.subject: Multiple group measurement invariance
parts:
Dear all

For the validation of a professional development scale we did a CFA to check for multiple group measurement invariance (men vs women).

 

We did a configural, metric, scalar and factor means comparison but I have to admit that the output is quite difficult for me to understand... Not really my cup of tea. I am still exploring these tests. 

 

Could somebody possibly shed more light on the interpretation of the results?

 

I think that indeed the scale works equally well for men and women but if I look at the last page (12)  I don’t really know what to make out of the chi square difference test and the fit measures… On the internet there is a lot about how to do these tests but not on the interpretation of them. I added a file of our results.

 

Thank you very much!

Brent

messages.author: 89492f4724ac0082
messages.subject: Re: Multiple group measurement invariance
parts:
Hi Brent,

The summary outputs for each model contain general information (# observations for each group, estimators, df, etc.), fit measures (Chi-square for each group, CFI, RMSEA, etc.), and then the parameter estimates. The output of "measurementInvariance" contains a summary of the fit measures normally used for testing invariance at each level, e.g. CFI and RMSEA. The values of CFI and RMSEA in the table output of "measurementInvariance" are the same found in the model summaries.

Looking at the fit measures in your output of "measurementInvariance" I see that RMSEA is above the limit for acceptable fit (0.08) right at the configural level. The Chi-square results in the summary of the configural model show that the misfit comes mostly from group one (Chi-square = 70.758), but your sample is also biased towards that group (208 observations against 109).

To improve the fit measures of the configural model and be able to proceed to the other tests, perhaps you could delete some of the items  loading on your pd factor. You can use the modification indices to select them.

The summary outputs show that you allowed item .PROFDEVC_SQ007 to be correlated with item  PROFDEVC_SQ008 and item .PROFDEVC_SQ001 to be correlated with item  PROFDEVC_SQ003. What was the reason for doing so?

Best regards,

Carlos M. Lemos

messages.author: 7797bf0ba5995253
messages.subject: Re: Multiple group measurement invariance
parts:
Dear Carlos

Thank you for your answer. 

We allowed these correlations because earlier tests pertaining to our model showed that their modification indices  were quite high.

Best regards
Brent
